title: Prime-power quotients of a Cohen ring are flat
statement: Let $p$ be a prime, let $\Lambda$ be a Cohen ring [def-weil-pbc-cohen-ring], and let $n\geq0$. For every algebra structure of $\Lambda/(p^n)$ over $\mathbf Z/p^n\mathbf Z$, the module $\Lambda/(p^n)$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map].

source.place: Algebra, Tag 0329 induction step; checked at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0329

proof.text: The Cohen-ring domain has characteristic zero: if the prime p vanished, its maximal ideal (p) would be zero and the DVR a field. If a different prime q vanished, Bezout for p and q would make p a unit in its maximal ideal. Therefore no prime vanishes, giving characteristic zero by Mathlib CharZero.charZero_iff_forall_prime_ne_zero.

source.place: Algebra, Tag 0329 induction step; checked at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0329

proof.text: The integer action on the characteristic-zero domain is torsion-free. The PID torsion-free flatness instance gives Module.Flat ℤ Λ.

source.place: Algebra, Tag 0329 induction step; checked at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0329

proof.text: Let I=(p^n) in ℤ and J=IΛ. Use Algebra.TensorProduct.quotIdealMapEquivQuotTensor and Module.Flat.baseChange to prove that Λ/J is flat over ℤ/I.

source.place: Algebra, Tag 0329 induction step; checked at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0329

proof.text: Compute J=(p^n) in Λ. Transport flatness along Int.quotientSpanNatEquivZMod and Ideal.quotEquivOfEq. The resulting ring map equals any given ZMod-algebra map because both preserve integer casts and ZMod.intCast_surjective covers every element.

theorem cohenRing_mod_pow_flat
    (p : ℕ) (Λ : Type u) [CommRing Λ] (hΛ : IsCohenRing p Λ) (n : ℕ)
    [Algebra (ZMod (p ^ n)) (Λ ⧸ Ideal.span {(p : Λ) ^ n})] :
